sampling_model.design: Balanced \(K=K_N\)-arm product experiment with \(N=Km\) and fixed \(d>4\).
sampling_model.units: For arm \(k\), \(X_{k1},\ldots,X_{km}\) are identically distributed from the arbitrary marginal \(P_k\) on \(\mathbb B_d\); all arm samples are independent.
sampling_model.treatment: The observed experiment supplies one independent sample from each potential-outcome marginal and leaves the within-unit \(K\)-world coupling unidentified.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each marginal is estimated empirically. No density, smoothness, joint-mixability, known nuisance, or centered-variance substitution is imposed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Proposition 3.6 places a binary covariate-aware mirror-transport lower bound between unconditional and conditional transport, while Theorem 4.3 gives its quadratic-cost plug-in rate under smooth strongly convex Brenier potentials.
The paper proves continuity of binary conditional transport under adapted Wasserstein distance and derives a direct nonparametric estimator with a convergence rate.
The paper gives a smooth-density wavelet estimator and asymptotic normality for binary conditional transport with quadratic cost.
Theorem 22 gives the two-margin all-estimator lower bound \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) for quadratic cost.
Theorem 2.2 converts binary \(c\)-transform entropy into two-margin empirical transport rates.
Theorem 3.1 gives uniformly valid one-sided inference from any dual-feasible estimated pair in randomized experiments.
The paper constructs finite-sample intervals for sliced Wasserstein distance and bounds their length near the minimax rate.
The paper gives necessary and sufficient joint-mixability conditions for selected classes of univariate distributions.
Donsker dual classes yield two-margin empirical optimal-transport limits given by suprema of Gaussian processes.
Upper and lower Wasserstein dimensions determine multiscale empirical-measure approximation rates.
Quadratic negative-dependence objectives are optimized for selected identical scalar margins admitting a joint mix.
The ordered modulus gives one-sided minimax expected-length optimality for linear Gaussian regression functionals.
Optimal multi-margin dual potentials may be chosen as a simultaneously conjugate family.
Two-mode stability controls regular Monge maps for barycentric and uniformly concave sum costs.
Fixed-finite-support multi-sample optimal-transport values admit weak limits and bootstrap tests.
Sharp two-arm randomization-variance bounds yield asymptotically conservative narrow Wald intervals under unequal allocation.
Generic discrete multimarginal transport approximation has exponential tensor dependence in the number of margins.
Generic pairwise-interaction multimarginal transport is computationally hard.

body.tldr: The lower endpoint \(L(\mathbf P)\) is the sharp causal second moment compatible with \(K\) observed potential-outcome marginals, not the centered variance residual. Gao--Ge--Qian identify this endpoint and bound its empirical plug-in risk, but their \(d>4\) theorem leaves both the arm-count frontier and the all-estimator logarithmic gap open, and their support-geometry proof does not exploit fixed dimension. The core derives the exact residual envelope \(\min\{K,d\}/K^2\), a sharp \(2\sqrt{\min\{K,d\}}\) diameter for optimal sums, and a strictly tighter plug-in upper bound, settling root-\(N\) minimax estimation and honest one-sided excess length for \(K\gtrsim N^{1/4}\). The answer-open kernel operationalizes the remaining frontier with a named rational finite-support simultaneous-marginal family whose product-law indistinguishability, endpoint separation, and reduced-cost slack against every rematching column are finite computations; failure of that lower route points to a shared-complexity theorem for jointly conjugate potentials. A fixed-dimensional primal--dual certificate makes the statistical claim computable. The STAR audit is conditional on a known finite outcome bound, an explicit affine scale, an i.i.d. superpopulation law, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling, and it does not validate the native \(161/37/36\) calculation.

project_justification.gap: Gao--Ge--Qian Theorem 1 gives a high-dimensional empirical bound with term \(K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\), while Proposition 2 prints a two-margin lower term with \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) and does not establish uniform one-sided coverage or optimal expected excess length. Manole--Niles-Weed leave the same logarithmic all-estimator gap already at two margins. Two-margin entropy transfer and limit theory do not control a growing tuple of jointly conjugate potentials.
project_justification.niche: The squared-sum cost has shared fixed-dimensional geometry that is absent from generic transport bounds: all potentials obey one constraint, and optimal coupling atoms can be exchanged in arbitrary coordinate subsets. At the same time, a lower construction must survive every alternative multi-arm rematching, so neither a union bound nor a two-margin embedding can decide the rate.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the sharp deterministic residual and support-diameter theorems, uses common-support interpolation to tighten the plug-in rate, settles the large-arm root-\(N\) estimation and one-sided length regimes, and poses the precise coupled-complexity dichotomy whose resolution yields the exact all-\(K\) frontier. Its finite-support handle makes indistinguishability, endpoint separation, and resistance to every rematching column explicit certification targets. The procedure returns a primal--dual numerical bracket, and the STAR audit declares the known bound, affine scaling, superpopulation law, randomization, and balanced subsampling.

body.related_work: Gao, Ge, and Qian define exactly \(L(\mathbf P)\) in their equation (4), prove the balanced-sample upper rate in Theorem 1, and claim minimax optimality only for \(d\le4\); their Discussion leaves \(d>4\) open. Their supplement localizes each dual potential separately after one-coordinate support exchanges. The upper theorem changes both steps: arbitrary-subset exchanges produce dimension-saturated optimal-sum geometry, and common-support interpolation yields jointly normalized concave potentials. The two-margin identity in Lemma 5 is only a definitional sanity reduction and is not counted toward novelty. Manole and Niles-Weed's Theorem 22 supplies the closest all-estimator lower architecture, but its fuzzy-hypothesis argument gives \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) for the two-margin quadratic cost. Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn's ICML 2025 Proposition 3.6 and Theorem 4.3 study binary covariate-aware causal transport: a mirror-covariate relaxation interpolates between unconditional and conditional bounds and has a plug-in rate under regular Brenier potentials. Their AISTATS 2026 follow-up proves continuity of binary conditional transport under adapted Wasserstein distance and analyzes a direct nonparametric estimator. Their 2026 smooth-density preprint gives a wavelet estimator and asymptotic normality for quadratic binary conditional transport. These covariate-assisted results inform the causal-transport framing but neither tighten nor represent the unconditional arbitrary-margin endpoint with growing \(K\), so the comparator table records them as informed-by rather than extension targets. Hundrieser, Staudt, and Munk show that a binary \(c\)-transform transfers entropy between two potentials; the multi-margin transform depends on all other potentials and has no corresponding tuple contraction. Hundrieser, Klatt, Staudt, and Munk characterize two-margin empirical-cost limits under Donsker dual classes, not the growing-arm high-dimensional transition. Han and Zhu's 2026 two-mode stability theorem assumes regular Monge structure and treats barycentric or uniformly concave sum costs, not the arbitrary-margin repulsive endpoint or its statistical risk. Weed and Bach supply the multiscale quantization background but estimate an empirical measure in Wasserstein distance rather than a smooth MOT value. Wang and Wang characterize zero residual for selected scalar families, while Wang's survey identifies vector mixability and attainable sum laws as open. Koike, Lin, and Wang analyze identical scalar margins and do not cover arbitrary heterogeneous vector laws. Manole, Balakrishnan, and Wasserman derive near-minimax interval lengths for sliced Wasserstein distance through one-dimensional quantiles. Ji, Lei, and Spector derive model-agnostic validity from dual feasibility but no all-arm minimax expected-length converse. Armstrong and Kolesar's ordered modulus motivates the one-sided decision criterion in a linear Gaussian model. Cheryala, Alaya, and Bouzebda establish multi-margin dual attainment and conjugacy without statistical capacity bounds, and Kravtsova treats fixed finite supports rather than arbitrary unit-ball marginals or growing \(K\). Aronow, Green, and Lee prove sharp unequal-allocation variance inference for two arms; their multiple-treatment remark does not supply the unequal three-margin result. Angrist, Lang, and Oreopoulos provide the randomized STAR experiment. Gao--Ge--Qian's application uses native cell sizes \(161,37,36\); the balanced theorem applies to the audit only under the declared i.i.d. superpopulation law, known bound, affine scale, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The exact small-arm rate remains answer-open. The finite-support perturbation template is operational, but no choice of its support, signed directions, amplitudes, and hypothesis priors is asserted to attain the missing rate: endpoint separation, product-law indistinguishability, and reduced-cost resistance to every rematching column must be established together. The only settled lower helper is the definitional two-margin specialization scaled by \(K^{-2}\), whereas the improved upper theorem can retain a \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\) term; tensoring two-margin gadgets in fixed dimension does not bridge that factor because alternative arms can rematch. The official Gao--Ge--Qian supplement also asserts \(\sum_k\|y_1(k)-y_2(k)\|_2^2\le2K\) from unit-ball support, although the displayed support condition alone yields \(4K\); this core therefore re-proves the needed support theorem and does not borrow that step. The certified computation theorem is fixed-dimensional and polynomial in \((K/\epsilon)^d\), not a claim of generic polynomial-time exact MOT. The STAR audit discards observations, depends on a known outcome bound and a superpopulation model, and does not reproduce the published numerical tightening.
body.honest_scope: Every numbered statement is to be proved. The exact residual envelope, optimal-sum diameter, improved empirical upper bound, large-arm minimax claims, computation certificate, and STAR audit are presolve-supported but not treated as established. The exact all-\(K\) rate and the honest one-sided converse are the principal open content; the named simultaneous-marginal family is a construction handle whose required endpoint separation and rematching resistance are not assumed. The proposal makes no density or smoothness assumption, fixes \(d>4\), requires \(m=N/K\to\infty\), and preserves the uncentered second-moment endpoint \(L\). When only two margins are nondegenerate, Lemma 5 is definitionally the ordinary quadratic two-margin transport cost and serves only as a sanity reduction; when \(K\) is fixed, the known sandwich retains the Manole--Niles-Weed logarithmic gap; when \(K\gtrsim N^{1/4}\), Theorems 8 and 9 reduce both decision risks to the familiar root-\(N\) mean problem. For the hypercube special case, Proposition 4 gives zero for even \(K\) and \(K^{-2}\) for odd \(K\), including \(1/9\) at \(K=3,d=5\). The empirical STAR audit is conditional on its declared known-bound scaling and i.i.d. randomized-subsampling model and makes no claim for the native unequal-count computation.
